title: Stability Guardrails and KPI Flightplan for Activation
content:
Context:
We need a compact, actionable flightplan that ties the product activation roadmap to measurable stability guardrails. This doc is the product-ops canonical working draft for the next 6-week low-touch rollout (feature flag ramp to 50%). It focuses on signal thresholds, rapid mitigation playbooks, and a pragmatic KPI tracker that SRE, Product, and CS can use without heavy tooling edits.

Purpose:
- Reduce ambiguity about "go/no-go" signals during ramp phases.
- Give on-call and PMs a short checklist and remediation steps for the 0->50% rollout window.
- Surface early regressions with clear owners and timelines.

Summary (one-paragraph):
We will perform a controlled activation across three phases (alpha internal, beta 0-10%, ramp 10-50%). Primary KPIs are request latency P95, error rate (user-facing and infra), and quality regressions (prompt-level failure rate). Each KPI has an explicit guardrail with automated alerts and an owner who must decide within the stated SLA. If any guardrail trips, start the graded mitigation ladder (rate limit, rollback partial, full rollback).

Rollout Phases:
1) Alpha (week -2 to 0): internal + internal tools only. Validate telemetry, smoke tests, and synthetic load.
2) Beta (week 0 to 2): 0-10% traffic. Manual monitoring cadence: twice-daily check-ins.
3) Ramp (week 2 to 6): 10-50% traffic. Monitoring cadence: hourly for first 48h, then every 4h if stable.

Primary KPIs and Guardrails (owner | threshold | response SLA):
- Latency P95 | owner: Marcus Nguyen | threshold: > 450ms for 10m window | response SLA: 30m to acknowledge, 2h to mitigate
- Error rate (5xx infra) | owner: Zoe Kim | threshold: > 0.8% sustained over 5m | response SLA: 15m acknowledge, 1h mitigate
- User-facing failures (incorrect structured outputs / parsing errors) | owner: Product PM (Lina) | threshold: > 2% on sample prompts over 30m | response SLA: 1h acknowledge, rolling back to previous model config in 4h if unresolved
- Token cost spike (per-request unit cost) | owner: Finance liaison (Elena) | threshold: +30% baseline across 1h | response SLA: 2h evaluation, cap traffic if needed
- Downstream SLO breach (dependent service) | owner: SRE lead (Ravi) | threshold: downstream latency > 200ms increase or >1% errors | response SLA: 15m to engage dependency owner

KPI Tracker snapshot (plain table to paste to spreadsheets):
DATE,PHASE,TRAFFIC%,LAT_P95_MS,ERROR_RATE_5XX,USER_FAIL_RATE,COST_PER_1000,NOTES
2025-01-24,alpha,internal,120,0.0%,0.0%,$0.00,smoke tests
2025-01-31,beta,5,160,0.12%,0.4%,$1.12,initial beta; minor parser flakiness
2025-02-03,beta,10,180,0.15%,0.9%,$1.20,monitoring cadence increased

Readiness Checklist (pre-roll action items):
- [ ] Canary image pinned and immutable; rollback tag validated (owner: Release Eng)
- [ ] Synthetic test deck expanded to include 50 prompt families (owner: Applied ML)
- [ ] Tracing hooks + token-level cost telemetry enabled in prod (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Runbook ready in Ops PagerDuty escalation policy; contact list verified (owner: Product-ops)
- [ ] Customer-impact matrix prepared for CS (owner: Customer Success)

Operational Playbook (if guardrail trips):
Step 0 — Acknowledge: owner triages and posts status to #prod-activation within SLA.
Step 1 — Mitigate: limit traffic to flagged bucket (10% isolate) and enable prefix caching where applicable.
Step 2 — Stabilize: apply temporary rate-limits or reduce concurrency on impacted route. If cost spike, cap new sessions.
Step 3 — Remediate: apply quick rollback to previous model/config or adjust quantization profile. If user-quality regression, swap to conservative model variant.
Step 4 — Postmortem: 72-hour internal doc with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and follow-ups assigned.

Escalation matrix (fast reference):
- Sev2 (impacting large cohort / major latency): SRE on-call -> SRE lead -> Eng manager -> CTO+PM sync within 2h
- Sev1 (platform down or major data loss): Immediate all-hands paging + exec notification

Monitoring and Dashboards (must-haves):
- P95 latency by route, by model variant (1m,5m,15m windows)
- Error rate heatmap with root-cause tagging (model vs infra vs downstream)
- Quality drift indicator: daily sample of 500 requests via golden prompt set
- Cost telemetry: tokens per request, per-route cost, cumulative spend vs baseline

Signals to watch (early-warning heuristics):
- Small but consistent increases in parsing failures across multiple prompts (signals model drift)
- Token usage per session rising >10% vs baseline (possible prompt change or bug)
- Concurrent requests spiked in a single client token range (client misconfiguration)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we want automatic rollback on user_fail_rate >3% for more than 30m? pros/cons discussed; needs Exec sign-off.
- Confirm if Finance wants daily burn alert at +20% or weekly only.
- Add additional synthetic tests for rare long-tail prompts (owner: Applied ML).

Quick links and references:
- Activation runbook (Confluence ID: PRODOPS-activation-runbook)
- Current rollout PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/46
- PagerDuty schedule: pd://product-ops-schedule

Notes (informal):
- This isn't the final playbook; it's intentionally terse so on-call can act quickly. Expect iterations after beta.
- Keep the golden prompt set trimmed to highest-value prompts only to reduce noise in quality signals.

Decision log (short):
- 2025-01-10: agreed on incremental ramp (0->10->50) and hourly checks for first 48h (owners: product-ops + SRE)
- 2025-01-22: approved synthetic deck and tracing scope (owners: applied-ml + observability)
